rationale.complete: Round 1 done: card and predictions before data, synthetic on the real skeleton (6 worlds x 3 amplitudes) that exposed three biased or powerless estimators, Amendment 1 before real data, 27 kickoffs x 4 configurations, natives G51 and NE38, per-period estimates, confirm.py frozen and dry-run (reproduces stand-ins), not run.
rationale.faithfulness: HH368's relaxation picture is not what the data show: 74% of rising agents adopt within the read-out call, beyond every synthetic relaxation world. The call-rate slope itself is inconclusive (power ~0.35 at the observed rise), and the spike-then-decay description is post hoc. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D0 E1 F2 G1 H1 I1.
rationale.usefulness: Operator-relevant: goal adoption happens at the first read-out call, so cadence is not a lever for adoption speed; early statements overstate adoption. The instrument lessons (collapse and t0-origin clock tests are fooled by read-out gating) transfer to any message-delivered field.

one_line: No catch-up to time: agents adopt a new goal within their read-out call (74% of 152 rising agents), then the kickoff's salience decays over ~64 calls; the call-rate slope is inconclusive (+0.59 [-0.45, +1.75]).

models.note: overdamped catch-up on the call clock not seen; step at read-out

v2.claim: An agent adopts a new goal within its read-out call, not by gradual catch-up: 74% of 152 rising agents are at their day-1 plateau in the first statement after reading the kickoff (relaxation worlds give ≤ 0.20); alignment then decays from about 2.4× to 1× the plateau over about 64 calls
